text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Peru guerillas storm Japanese envoy's residence during VIP reception and and take 200 hostage.
- United States warns foreign telecom firms to lower the cost of international telephone calls or risk losing a lot of money.
- Three former board members of Amcol Holdings charged with failing to act honestly in their duties as directors.
- Developers will bid cautiously for latest batch of 99-year residential parcels released by the Government.
- Scotts Investments and Yusuf Jumabhoy propose three new non-executive directors be added to Scotts Holdings' board.
- Singapore Regional Index Fund raises Singapore $249 million at end of its month-long launch period yesterday.
- Hong kong Stock Exchange draws controversial plans for negotiated commissions.
- Singapore $2 billion petrochemical complex expects to report poor earnings this year, squeezed by weak product prices and high raw material costs.
- Ossia International, which listed last month on main board, plans to list its retail arm of World of Sports.
- U.S. dollar denominated Osprey Maritime starts trading in Singapore dollars from Thursday with added bonus.
- Hong kong-based CM Telecom International sees its group net profit rise just five percent to Hong Kong $43.7 million.
- Listed GP Batteries International posts a 14.3 percent rise in interim net profit to Singapore $12.78 million.
- Causeway Investment Ltd secures another extension to repay about Singapore $700,000 in shareholders' loans.
